expectations.text: Produces options that differ in mechanism rather than being variations on 'make the meeting more engaging'
expectations.evidence: Genuine mechanism differences present: 'Try a different cadence ... Quarterly-but-excellent plus a strong written monthly update', 'Put something at stake. A live decision', 'Delay the recording ... if the recording is posted instantly, live attendance has no advantage'. Weaker than with_skill: roughly half the list ('Shrink it', 'Rotate the stage', 'Unfiltered Q&A', 'Move the news out') is format or content improvement.

expectations.text: At least one option questions the premise — whether the all-hands should exist in this form, or whether attendance is the right thing to optimise
expectations.evidence: 'Monthly is an awkward interval ... Quarterly-but-excellent plus a strong written monthly update beats a mediocre monthly ritual. This is worth considering seriously rather than treating cadence as fixed.' Plus 'Attendance is a useful thermometer; don't break the thermometer' — treating turnout as signal rather than target.

expectations.text: Does not treat declining attendance as purely a content-quality problem
expectations.evidence: Opens with three separated causes — low information value, low stakes / no consequence, friction — and explicitly notes 'recording always available so live attendance is strictly dominated'.

expectations.text: Proportionate: under roughly 800 words, no heavy scaffolding for a light question
expectations.evidence: wc -w = 604 words, essentially identical to the with_skill run (602). Four light headings, no process apparatus.

expectations.text: MODE CHECK: did NOT spawn parallel generator subagents or run web research for this
expectations.evidence: user_notes.md line 1: 'MODE: none'. metrics.json: total_tool_calls = 3, subagents_spawned = 0, web_searches = 0.

expectations.text: Surfaces at least one non-obvious diagnosis of WHY attendance falls, not just a list of fixes
expectations.evidence: 'Cheapest way to tell them apart: look at who is missing. If it's clustered by team or time zone, it's friction. If it's spread evenly and skews senior, it's value. If newer people attend and long-tenured people don't, it's "I've seen this movie ten times".' Also names the substitution effect (instant recording strictly dominates live).
